evals.prompt: Grill my plan before I build it. I want to add a dark mode to the settings page of a small web app: a toggle in the header, the choice saved per browser, and charts recolored to match. Write round 1 as the queue JSON file and build it into the HTML page. Do not build the feature. Then tell me which decisions you held for later rounds.
evals.expected_output: A round-1 queue JSON and a built page whose frontier decisions about appearance each carry one visual per option, with dependent decisions held for later rounds.
expectations: The output lists decisions the plan leaves open or assumes, beyond the three things the plan states
Round 1 asks at least one decision about how the page or the charts look, and each such decision has one image or html visual per option, each bound to its option with the option key
At least one decision that depends on another open decision is named as held for a later round, in the queue JSON or the reply, instead of being asked in round 1
Every open decision in round 1 has two to four options, a recommendation or an explicit taste call, a door and a blast radius
build.py exits without an error when the grader re-runs it on the queue JSON

evals.prompt: Grill this plan. An upload job moves through queued, uploading, done and failed. A failed job retries up to 3 times, the user can cancel at any time, and a cancel during a retry should not leave a half-uploaded file. Write round 1 as the queue JSON file and build it into the HTML page. Then tell me which decisions you held for later rounds.
evals.expected_output: A round-1 queue JSON and a built page where the state-model questions carry an interactive html demo the user can click through.
expectations: Every round-1 decision about how the job moves through its states, or about what a cancel or a retry leaves behind, has its own html visual with interactive set to true where the user runs the same steps under each of that decision's options and sees the resulting job state
The interactive visual has no option key
The decisions include what happens when cancel arrives during a retry
No decision asks the user for a fact the agent could have reasoned out or looked up, including what the plan's own words already say, such as the number of retries
build.py exits without an error when the grader re-runs it on the queue JSON

evals.prompt: Grill me on a policy for my open-source repo: should stale issues be closed automatically, and if so after how long and with what message? Write round 1 as the queue JSON file and build it into the HTML page. Then tell me which decisions you held for later rounds.
evals.expected_output: A round-1 queue JSON and a built page that asks whether to auto-close first, holds the timing and message for after that answer, and shows each option's effect as text.
expectations: The decision on whether to auto-close is asked in round 1
The timing and the message decisions are named as held for a later round, in the queue JSON or the reply, because they depend on the auto-close decision
No round-1 decision depends on how another round-1 decision is answered; for example, whether pull requests get the same treatment is held until the auto-close decision is settled
Each round-1 option shows what it would put in place, such as the rule or the message text, as a visual
The decision whose blast radius covers every open issue has confirm set to true or a one-way door
build.py exits without an error when the grader re-runs it on the queue JSON

evals.prompt:
Continue grilling my repo's stale-issue policy. Round 1 asked close-scope ("Which issues may a bot close for inactivity?", options no-auto-close, waiting-on-reporter, all-inactive) and add-template ("Add an issue template that asks for repro steps?", options add-template, skip). It held include-prs ("Should the same policy close pull requests?"), stale-timing ("How many quiet days before closing?") and close-message ("What does the close comment say?"), each blocked by close-scope. My answers:

queue: stale-policy  round: 1
close-scope: no-auto-close
add-template: skip
evals.expected_output: The held decisions drop out because nothing will be auto-closed, nothing is left open, so the agent states the settled plan and waits for confirmation instead of asking a round 2 or building anything.
expectations: include-prs, stale-timing and close-message are removed as moot rather than asked in a round 2
No round-2 HTML page is built
The reply states the settled plan in a few lines and asks the user to confirm it
No workflow, config or other repo file implementing the policy is created

evals.prompt:
Continue grilling my upload plan. Round 1 asked storage ("Where does an upload write while it is in progress?", options stage-then-commit, write-in-place). It held chunk-size ("Which chunk size?", options 5mb, 16mb, 64mb), blocked by storage and by median-file-size, a fact a subagent is measuring from last month's upload logs. The subagent has not reported yet.

My answers:

queue: upload  round: 1
storage: stage-then-commit
evals.expected_output: With chunk-size still waiting on the file-size measurement, the agent builds no page and says it is waiting for that fact.
expectations: No round-2 HTML page is built
The reply says the agent is waiting for the median file size before asking chunk-size
The reply does not ask the user to pick a chunk size or to supply the file size

evals.prompt:
Continue grilling my upload plan. Round 1 asked storage ("Where does an upload write while it is in progress?", options stage-then-commit, write-in-place). It held chunk-size ("Which chunk size?", options 5mb, 16mb, 64mb), blocked by storage and by median-file-size, a fact a subagent is measuring from last month's upload logs. The subagent has now reported: the median upload is 180 MB and the 95th percentile is 2.1 GB.

My answers:

queue: upload  round: 1
storage: stage-then-commit
evals.expected_output: The measurement unblocks chunk-size, so the agent builds round 2 asking it, with the measurement as evidence.
expectations: A round-2 queue JSON asks chunk-size, and storage is not asked again
chunk-size carries the 180 MB median or the 2.1 GB 95th percentile as evidence
build.py exits without an error when the grader re-runs it on the queue JSON
